title: Browser Agents and Long-Horizon Web Tasks

questions.question: Which visible-text signal does sanitizer explicitly recognize on the forum page?
options: The phrase IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS and its exfiltration request
Any occurrence of the word release
Every URL fragment
Only an HTML heading
questions.explanation: The sanitizer rules match the instruction override, the post-to-/api/exfil pattern, and the request to use the same auth.

questions.question: Why does sanitizer alone miss the URL-fragment injection?
options: It never reads HTML
Its rules inspect the HTML string but do not inspect the page URL
It blocks all fragments before reading them
The fragment is converted into a user-origin action
questions.explanation: sanitizer receives html only. The fragment contains /api/exfil in url, which is appended to context later and is outside those regex checks.

questions.question: What does the R/W boundary do when the agent follows a page-origin /api/exfil instruction?
options: It rewrites the endpoint to /api/post
It sanitizes the secret body
It blocks the write because content_origin is page, not user
It approves it after checking the URL scheme
questions.explanation: rw_boundary_allows returns true only for content_origin == 'user', so a write selected from fetched page content returns no write executed.

questions.question: What happens for the benign page under the rw_boundary defense?
options: The page is always rejected as untrusted
The agent posts the session token
The sanitizer strips the release notes
The requested user-origin comment is posted to /api/post with body ok
questions.explanation: No injection changes the default endpoint or body, and content_origin remains user, so the boundary permits the /api/post action.

questions.question: What does defense='both' do for the visible-text injection?
options: It posts only the intended /api/post comment: sanitizer strips the visible payload, and any remaining page-origin write would be rejected
It posts the secret because the URL is trusted
It ignores the page and posts to /api/exfil
It disables the user request
questions.explanation: The sanitizer removes the visible injection before context construction, so the default user-origin /api/post action remains; the boundary independently blocks any page-origin write.

questions.question: What is the outcome for the URL-fragment page with defense='sanitizer'?
options: The fragment is caught and no write occurs
The URL is not sanitized, so the naive decision path posts SENSITIVE to /api/exfil
The R/W boundary blocks it automatically
The page is treated as user-origin because it has no visible injection
questions.explanation: sanitizer does not inspect URLs; /api/exfil remains in context, so the agent selects the page-origin exfiltration write and sanitizer alone does not block it.
